summary: Highly implementable: the CAS publication, the outcome types and the checkout synchronization are specified. Remaining gaps are whether kb init commits taps.dhall (conflicting with ADR 0015) and which refusal a stale saved candidate produces.

questions.text: ADR 0015 says kb init writes the first-party taps.dhall declaration in the initial commit, while ADR 0012's initialization publishes only the RootStore export and synchronizes only root/.
questions.reason: Committing it needs a second subtree replacement, wider synchronization and a rule for an existing taps.dhall. ADR 0015 says '`kb init` writes the first-party declaration as part of the initial KB commit', and ADR 0012 says '...exports the validated root through RootStore ... and synchronizes only `root/`'.

questions.text: Does a Ready workspace whose inputs no longer match its saved candidate get refused as InvalidMaterial or WorkspaceChanged, and is that cheap check run before checkCandidate?
questions.reason: The two constructors carry different repair guidance, and the ordering decides whether every stale accept pays for full compilation. ADR 0012 says 'Missing, stale or rejected material is NotAccepted (InvalidMaterial ...)' but also defines 'WorkspaceChanged means the currently selected workspace no longer matches the captured input material'.

questions.text: What exactly does the pure empty initialization scaffold contain: module names, kb.dhall values, and recipe/example/plugin directories?
questions.reason: It must pass checkRoot, and its module naming shapes every first evolution's before/ copy and imports. ADR 0005 says 'This gives initialization an empty root without dummy fields', and ADR 0006 lists the manifest fields, but no ADR gives the scaffold files.

questions.text: Should acceptance and initialization refuse while a Git merge, cherry-pick or revert is in progress on the selected branch?
questions.reason: Advancing the ref under MERGE_HEAD leaves the user's merge state inconsistent. ADR 0012 checks only the branch selection ('refuse detached HEAD or a different checked-out branch') and overlapping root paths.

questions.text: In what order are NotReady, CheckoutMismatch, BaseMismatch, WorkspaceChanged and OverlappingEdits evaluated when several apply?
questions.reason: AcceptanceProblem reports a single problem, so the order decides the repair users and scripts see. ADR 0012 fixes only that NotReady is checked 'before candidate loading', and leaves the rest unordered.
